audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: the chart gave Darius 5 of 7 stages while Darius wins only 48.94% over 3296 games, and the '2+ items' stage said Darius even though the matchup's whole shape is that Nasus outscales.
audit.why: Losing the lane and winning the game is exactly this matchup. The mirror (nasus__darius.json) flips its own late stage to Nasus and its content layer already reads Nasus there; leaving Darius on this side would put the two pages in direct contradiction.
audit.corrected: Stage 7 (2+ items) flipped to Nasus at 4/10, with the why rewritten to say why: Wither plus a stacked Siphoning Strike wins the sidelane duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 chart entry carried a leaked LaTeX formula ('R = d + a 	imes Stacks') and said nothing about Fury of the Sands, which is the only thing that changes at 6 on his side.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health AND bonus Armour and Magic Resist. Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so only the Health half of that ult matters against your execute — a Nasus who pops R expecting his resists to save him still dies to a 5-stack Guillotine.
audit.corrected: Level 6 why now states the resists-do-nothing interaction and keeps the true-damage point.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing stated the two decisive ability interactions: Siphoning Strike only grows on a killing blow (so denied cannons are permanently deleted damage), and Fury of the Sands' armour/MR are irrelevant to Noxian Guillotine.
audit.why: Riot's Siphoning Strike text: it increases the power of future Siphoning Strikes 'if he slays his target' — denying the last hit, not the trade, is what starves him. Riot's R text lists bonus Health, Armour and Magic Resist; Darius's R is flagged trueDamage.
audit.corrected: Both interactions written into the do's, the level-6 stage and the wave block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. 'Long early cooldown' and 'bait it before committing' with no numbers.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1; Wither is 15s at rank 1. That eleven-second gap is the lane: if you open with the pull, his answer is back on cooldown before your engage is. The concrete rule is to make him spend Wither first.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block now gives both numbers and the eleven-second gap as the sequencing rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave (and the identical report[4].t) had an unrelated block spliced into the middle — 'Key Mechanical Cooldowns Darius E (Apprehend)... How Darius Wins Trades...' — duplicating the cooldowns and trading sections inside the wave text.
audit.why: It is visible corruption on the page and it displaces the only place the freeze plan can be explained, which in this matchup is the win condition.
audit.corrected: Spliced block replaced in-band with Nasus-specific freeze instruction: deny cannons, never slow-push into his tower, rebuild a broken freeze by tanking the wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two entries had bodies that did not match their headings — 'Deny his Q stacks' described Wither, and 'Fight late when he's stacked' described burning your own Apprehend.
audit.why: Both headings name a mechanic the body never explains.
audit.corrected: Bodies replaced with the killing-blow stacking rule and the Wither-plus-R duel math respectively.

edits.before: You stay a side-lane terror but fall off vs grouped teams. Look for flank pulls in fights; one reset chain can win the game.
edits.after: A stacked Nasus wins the straight sidelane duel — Wither guts your stick and his Q one-shots. Group, flank for pulls, and end it.

edits.before: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks, bypassing defensive items completely. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands gives him bonus HP, Armour and MR, but Noxian Guillotine is true damage — only the HP half counts. Bleed him to 5 stacks and the execute still lands through his ult.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Bait it before committing. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Nasus Wither: 15s at rank 1 and his only kite — make him spend it, then commit. Darius E (Apprehend): 26s at rank 1, eleven seconds longer than Wither. Open with the pull and his answer is back before your engage is, so hold it for his step-up to a cannon rather than throwing it into the wave. Darius Ghost: your lethal enabler through the Wither slow — keep it for the run-down, never the walk-up.

edits.before: His only kite. Bait it before committing. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Siphoning Strike only grows on a killing blow — deny the cannon and that damage never exists.

edits.before: Your committal tool is the lane — burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: R adds HP and resists, Wither guts your attack speed — after two items the sidelane duel belongs to him.

edits.before: Best wave: your highest priority is maintaining a slow-building freeze locked directly outside your turret range. This completely denies them the safety of a short lane, leaves them highly exposed to devastating jungle collapses, and grants you an incredibly long runway to activate Ghost and run them down the lane the exact millisecond they waste an essential safety mechanism. Key Mechanical Cooldowns Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane. How Darius Wins Trades Look for them to walk forward to secure a critical minion last hit. Step up instantly, land an auto-attack directly into a fast Crippling Strike (W) reset, and use the heavy slow to step back out of their counter-abilities. If they panic and waste their primary mobility or crowd control tool, activate Ghost immediately, pull them back with Apprehend, and stack your passive to full for an easy execution loop. Worst wave: shoved to his tower with Apprehend and Ghost down. Crash timing: only crash to reset, take plates, or set up a dive — never shove on autopilot.
edits.after: Best wave: your highest priority is maintaining a slow-building freeze locked directly outside your turret range. This completely denies them the safety of a short lane, leaves them highly exposed to devastating jungle collapses, and grants you an incredibly long runway to activate Ghost and run them down the lane the exact millisecond they waste an essential safety mechanism. Against Nasus the freeze is not comfort, it is his stack count: every cannon he cannot walk to is damage permanently deleted from his late game, so hold the wave two or three casters outside your turret and last-hit at the latest possible moment. Never slow-push into his tower — a wave crashing under him is free Siphoning Strike stacks and a safe recall. If the freeze breaks, rebuild it by tanking the wave instead of clearing it. Nasus will shove the freeze off you with Spirit Fire, a 12-second, 650-range zone that also shreds your armour while you stand in it — step off it, and if the wave starts sliding toward him, thin the front rank yourself instead of letting it crash under his tower. Worst wave: shoved to his tower with Apprehend and Ghost down. Crash timing: only crash to reset, take plates, or set up a dive — never shove on autopilot.

The mirror flips its '2+ items' stage to Nasus, so this side's stage 7 is flipped to match — the two pages now agree that a stacked Nasus wins the late sidelane duel, which is why the aggregate favours him despite a losing lane. breakdown.wave and report[4].t on this entry had an unrelated block ('Key Mechanical Cooldowns... How Darius Wins Trades...') spliced into the middle of the wave text; both rewritten in-band with real Nasus freeze content.
